MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 7 1/4 L
   B. 7 1/2 L
   C. 7 L
   D. 7 3/4 L

2. A square has sides of 9 cm. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 27 cm
   B. 18 cm
   C. 81 cm
   D. 36 cm

3. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 by 3 by 2 blocks is 9 because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What is her mistake? (1 mark)
   A. She multiplied instead of adding
   B. She counted the faces
   C. She forgot the corners
   D. She added the numbers instead of multiplying

4. In a table, a row goes (1 mark)
   A. down the page
   B. diagonally only
   C. round in a circle
   D. across the page

5. Round 995 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 1000
   B. 900
   C. 1010
   D. 990

6. Which expression shows "twice a number p"? (1 mark)
   A. 2p
   B. p − 2
   C. p + 2
   D. p ÷ 2

7. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there? (1 mark)
   A. 730 bananas
   B. 610 bananas
   C. 630 bananas
   D. 620 bananas

8. Which decimal is the same as 1/2? (1 mark)
   A. 2.0
   B. 0.5
   C. 0.2
   D. 0.12

9. What is 61 ÷ 7? (1 mark)
   A. 8 remainder 6
   B. 7 remainder 12
   C. 8 remainder 5
   D. 9 remainder 5

10. One layer of a cuboid has 12 blocks and there are 2 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 22 blocks
   B. 14 blocks
   C. 24 blocks
   D. 36 blocks

11. What is 95 ÷ 4? (1 mark)
   A. 23 remainder 4
   B. 24 remainder 3
   C. 23 remainder 3
   D. 22 remainder 7

12. How many hours are in 5 days? (1 mark)
   A. 144 hours
   B. 120 hours
   C. 60 hours
   D. 300 hours

13. Change 2 m 45 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 2,450 cm
   B. 65 cm
   C. 245 cm
   D. 47 cm

14. How many minutes are in 8 hours? (1 mark)
   A. 192 minutes
   B. 540 minutes
   C. 800 minutes
   D. 480 minutes

15. What number is the Roman numeral II? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 5
   C. 6
   D. 2

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Using each of the digits 4, 0, 7 and 2 once, write the largest and the smallest 4-digit numbers you can make. (4 marks)

17. Kip faces west and makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which way does he face now? Explain. (3 marks)

18. Estimate 38 × 22 by rounding to the nearest ten. Then find the exact product. (4 marks)

19. Change 3.4 m to centimetres. (2 marks)

20. Change 3 hours to minutes and 2 days to hours. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #12 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 7 1/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 3 3/4 L + 3 1/2 L = 7 1/4 L.

2. D — 36 cm
   A square has four equal sides. 9 + 9 + 9 + 9 = 36.

3. D — She added the numbers instead of multiplying
   Volume = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 blocks.

4. D — across the page
   Rows go across and columns go down.

5. A — 1000
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 995 rounds to 1000.

6. A — 2p
   The key words tell us the operation. "twice a number p" is written 2p.

7. C — 630 bananas
   Multiply to find the total. The answer is 630 bananas.

8. B — 0.5
   1/2 = 5/10 = 0.5.

9. C — 8 remainder 5
   7 × 8 = 56 and 61 − 56 = 5. So 61 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 5. Check: 8 × 7 + 5 = 61.

10. C — 24 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 12 × 2 = 24 blocks.

11. C — 23 remainder 3
   4 × 23 = 92 and 95 − 92 = 3. So 95 ÷ 4 = 23 remainder 3. Check: 23 × 4 + 3 = 95.

12. B — 120 hours
   1 day = 24 hours, so 5 × 24 = 120 hours.

13. C — 245 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 2 × 100 = 200, and 200 + 45 = 245. So the answer is 245 cm.

14. D — 480 minutes
   1 hour = 60 minutes, so 8 × 60 = 480 minutes.

15. D — 2
   II stands for 2.

SECTION B
----
16. (4 marks)
   Answer: Largest: 7,420. Smallest: 2,047.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for 7,420 (digits in descending order). 2 marks for 2,047 (a 4-digit number cannot begin with 0).

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: North
   Working / marking points: Going clockwise the order is N, E, S, W and back to N (1 mark). West then a quarter turn clockwise gives north (1 mark). Answer north (1 mark).

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Estimate: 40 × 20 = 800. Exact: 836.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for rounding to 40 and 20, 1 mark for 800, 1 mark for 38 × 2 = 76 and 38 × 20 = 760, 1 mark for 836.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: 340 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 m = 300 cm and 0.4 m = 40 cm (1 mark). 300 + 40 = 340 cm (1 mark).

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: 180 minutes and 48 hours
   Working / marking points: 3 × 60 = 180 (1 mark); 2 × 24 = 48 (1 mark).
